items.title: Derrick Gardner interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 9, 2013
items.q: it was almost exactly a quote that I got from Ed Shaughnessy years ago

ctx.x: I think that there is music that can be written to be functional, you know, that serves a purpose. Like I was just talking to Doc Woods about this earlier today. He was talking about writing for films. And the music has to convey a mood and not take away from the dialogue that’s being conveyed in the film. Or background music at a restaurant, you know, it serves a purpose. But when you’re composing music to be really listened to, concertized music, or even when you’re improvising, I’m one that believes that you…

I had to chuckle because I read a quote of yours and it was almost exactly a quote that I got from Ed Shaughnessy years ago, and it was about if you look out there and at least some of the people aren’t moving or tapping your feet, you’re not doing your job.
You’re not doing your job, that’s right. Yeah. Yeah, Basie said the same thing. That’s right. That’s right.
